title: PWM + RC：最便宜的 DAC
summary: PWM 引脚只会 0 V 和 3.3 V。串一个电阻、并一个电容，就得到一个随占空比连续变化的直流电压，再让 ADC 自己读回来。
description: ESP32 的 PWM 引脚 → 10 kΩ → 结点 VDAC；VDAC 接 1 µF 到 GND，并接到一个 ADC1 引脚读回来。VDAC 的平均值 = 占空比 × 3.3 V，纹波随 PWM 频率升高而变小。测平均值、不同频率下的纹波，体会“纹波小”和“响应快”之间的取舍。

cards.title: 方波去哪了？
text: **PWM 引脚**（任意一个能输出的引脚）→ **`10 kΩ`** → 一列空孔，把这一列叫 **VDAC**。在「属性」里把引脚设成 **PWM**，**`1 kHz`**、**`50 %`**。
示波器 **CH1** 和**万用表**都接 VDAC。示波器上是方波，万用表显示什么？
再从 VDAC 到 GND 加一个 **`1 µF`** 电容，看 CH1：方波去哪了？

cards.title: 电容是一个慢慢装水的桶
text: - PWM 引脚要么是 3.3 V，要么是 0 V，从来不停在中间。能调的只是每个周期里 3.3 V 占多少时间：**占空比 D**。
![](fig:pwm)
- 电容是一个慢慢装水的桶：经过 10 kΩ 充电，它要 τ = RC = 10 ms 左右才装满，而引脚不到 1 ms 就翻一次。它跟不上，只好停在**平均值**附近。
- 平均值就是 3.3 V 占的时间比例：
- 代入 D = 60 %：$\bar V = 0.6 × 3.3 = 1.98$ V。D 怎么变，电压就沿一条直线跟着变——一个电阻加一个电容，就是一个**数模转换器（DAC）**。
![](fig:line)
- 剩下的小起伏叫**纹波**：引脚高时电容多充一点，低时多放一点。每个周期越短，它来不及动得越少。

cards.title: 让芯片自己读回来
text: - 保留电路，再加一根**跳线**：VDAC → 一个 **ADC1** 引脚（GPIO32–39），这个引脚设成 **ADC** 模式。芯片就能读回自己的输出。
- 点**「检查我的电路」**。检查会自己改占空比（25 / 50 / 75 %）和频率（100 Hz / 1 kHz / 10 kHz）。
- 回答测量题时，按题目在「属性」里设好占空比和频率：平均值用万用表读，纹波（Vpp）用示波器读。先预测，再读。

cards.title: 带走
text: - **PWM + RC = 便宜的 DAC**：平均值是 D × 3.3 V，RC 留下平均值、滤掉跳变。
- **纹波和速度要取舍**：RC 越大越平，但占空比一变，输出要约 5τ 才跟上。更好的办法是**提高 PWM 频率**：纹波变小，速度不变。
- 真实电路里的坑：VDAC 后面接负载，负载会和 10 kΩ 分压，电压被拉低——中间加一个 2.5 的电压跟随器。ESP32 还有两个真正的 8 位 DAC 引脚（GPIO25、GPIO26）；Blue Pill 的 STM32F103C8 一个都没有。

caption.text: D = 60 %：引脚 60 % 的时间在 3.3 V。VDAC 跟不上这么快的开关，只在平均值（虚线）附近小幅起伏（起伏画得夸张了）。

i18n.en: D = 60 %: the pin spends 60 % of the time at 3.3 V. VDAC cannot follow such fast switching and only wobbles around the average (dashed line; the wobble is exaggerated here).

caption.text: 平均值和占空比成正比：一条从 0 V 到 3.3 V 的直线。这就是一个 DAC。

i18n.en: The average is proportional to the duty cycle: a straight line from 0 V to 3.3 V. That is a DAC.

en.startNote: **Half-built**: the ESP32 (GPIO27 on 50 % PWM, GPIO34 on ADC), its GND wire and both probes are wired. **Why**: the board is a repeated skill; the RC low-pass *is* the DAC. **Your job**: R1 (10kΩ, GPIO27 → column 22), C1 (1µF, column 22 → GND), then column 22 to GPIO34 (j5).
en.title: PWM + RC: the cheapest DAC
en.summary: A PWM pin only knows 0 V and 3.3 V. Add a series resistor and a capacitor and you get a DC voltage that follows the duty cycle smoothly — and the ADC reads it back.
en.description: An ESP32 PWM pin → 10 kΩ → node VDAC; VDAC has 1 µF to GND and goes to an ADC1 pin to be read back. VDAC's average = duty × 3.3 V, and its ripple shrinks as the PWM frequency rises. Measure the average and the ripple at several frequencies, and see the trade-off between a small ripple and a fast response.
compare: - fc = 1/(2π × 10 kΩ × 1 µF) ≈ **16 Hz**, far below the 1 kHz PWM.
- 1 kHz, 50 %: 3.3 × 0.25 / (1000 × 10 ms) ≈ 82 mV (simulated **82 mV**); 1 kHz, 25 % and 75 %: D(1 − D) = 0.1875, ≈ 62 mV (simulated **62 mV**) — the ripple is largest at 50 %.

- 100 Hz, 50 %: τ is only one period; the approximation gives 0.83 V, the exact value 3.3 × tanh(T/4τ) ≈ 0.81 V (simulated **0.81 Vpp**, VDAC swings between 1.25 V and 2.05 V) — that is no longer "DC".
- 10 kHz, 50 %: ≈ 8 mV (simulated **8.2 mV**), more than one 12-bit ADC LSB (0.8 mV) but already quite flat.

- The ESP32 ADC pin draws no current, so there is no loading error; a 10 kΩ load on VDAC would form a divider with R1 and halve the average — buffer it with an op-amp follower if you need to drive something.

measurements.ask: 1 kHz, 25 %: multimeter DC range on VDAC to GND (the average)
measurements.explain: V̄ = D × 3.3 V ≈ 0.82 V (an ADC reading of about 1023).

measurements.ask: From your reading, the duty cycle D = V̄ / 3.3 V
measurements.explain: ≈ 0.25: the RC low-pass keeps only the PWM's DC component (its average), so PWM + RC is a DAC.

measurements.ask: 1 kHz, 50 %: VDAC's ripple Vpp on the scope
measurements.explain: For τ ≫ T the ripple ≈ 3.3 × D(1 − D) / (f·RC) = 3.3 × 0.25 / (1000 × 10 ms) ≈ 82 mV, largest at 50 %.
τ is only one period, so the approximation breaks down: 3.3 × tanh(T/4τ) ≈ 0.81 V, VDAC swings between about 1.25 V and 2.05 V — no longer DC.
Ripple ∝ 1/f: about 8 mV, a tenth of the 1 kHz value, with the same average. Raising the PWM frequency cuts ripple without slowing the output (τ is unchanged).

hints: PWM pin → 10 kΩ → VDAC; 1 µF from VDAC to GND; then a jumper from VDAC to an ADC1 pin (GPIO32–39).
Set the ADC pin to ADC mode and the other pin to PWM.
Average = duty × 3.3 V; a higher PWM frequency or a larger RC gives less ripple.
tests: 1 kHz, 50 %: sensible average, the largest ripple
100 Hz, 50 %: τ = T, a big ripple — no longer DC
10 kHz, 50 %: a tiny ripple, the same average

cards.title: Where did the square wave go?
text: **PWM pin** (any output pin) → **`10 kΩ`** → a free column; call that column **VDAC**. In **Properties** set the pin to **PWM**, **`1 kHz`**, **`50 %`**.
Put scope **CH1** and the **multimeter** on VDAC. The scope shows a square wave; what does the multimeter show?
Now add a **`1 µF`** capacitor from VDAC to GND and look at CH1: where did the square wave go?

cards.title: A capacitor is a slowly filling bucket
text: - A PWM pin is either at 3.3 V or at 0 V; it never stops in between. All you can set is how much of each period it spends at 3.3 V: the **duty cycle D**.
![](fig:pwm)
- A capacitor is a slowly filling bucket: charging through 10 kΩ it needs about τ = RC = 10 ms to fill, while the pin flips in under 1 ms. It cannot keep up, so it settles near the **average**.
- The average is just the share of time at 3.3 V:
- With D = 60 %: $\bar V = 0.6 × 3.3 = 1.98$ V. As D changes, the voltage follows along a straight line — one resistor and one capacitor make a **digital-to-analog converter (DAC)**.
![](fig:line)
- The small wobble left over is the **ripple**: the capacitor charges a little while the pin is high and drains a little while it is low. The shorter each period, the less it can move.

cards.title: Let the chip read it back
text: - Keep the circuit and add one **jumper**: VDAC → an **ADC1** pin (GPIO32–39), set to **ADC** mode. Now the chip can read its own output.
- Press **Check my circuit**. The check changes the duty (25 / 50 / 75 %) and the frequency (100 Hz / 1 kHz / 10 kHz) by itself.
- For each measurement question, set the duty and frequency in Properties as it says: read the average on the multimeter and the ripple (Vpp) on the scope. Predict first, then read.

cards.title: Take away
text: - **PWM + RC = a cheap DAC**: the average is D × 3.3 V; the RC keeps the average and filters out the jumps.
- **Ripple trades against speed**: a bigger RC is smoother, but after a duty change the output needs about 5τ to catch up. The better fix is a **higher PWM frequency**: less ripple, same speed.

- A real-world catch: a load on VDAC forms a divider with the 10 kΩ and pulls the voltage down — put the voltage follower from 2.5 in between. The ESP32 also has two true 8-bit DAC pins (GPIO25, GPIO26); the Blue Pill's STM32F103C8 has none.

tests.name: 100 Hz、50 %：τ = T，纹波很大，已经不是直流了

compare: - fc = 1/(2π × 10 kΩ × 1 µF) ≈ **16 Hz**，远低于 1 kHz 的 PWM 频率。
- 100 Hz、50 %：τ 只等于一个周期，近似公式给 0.83 V，精确值 3.3 × tanh(T/4τ) ≈ 0.81 V（仿真 **0.81 Vpp**，VDAC 在 1.25 V 和 2.05 V 之间摆）——这已经不是“直流”了。
- 10 kHz、50 %：≈ 8 mV（仿真 **8.2 mV**），比 12 位 ADC 的 1 LSB（0.8 mV）大，但已经很平了。
- ESP32 的 ADC 引脚不取电流，所以没有负载误差；如果 VDAC 后面接一个 10 kΩ 的负载，它和 R1 会组成分压，平均值会掉一半——要接负载就加一个 op-amp（运算放大器）跟随器。

measurements.ask: 1 kHz、25 %：万用表直流档测 VDAC 对 GND（平均值）
用你的读数反算占空比 D = V̄ / 3.3 V
measurements.explain: ≈ 0.25：RC 低通只留下 PWM 的直流分量（平均值），PWM + RC 就是一个 DAC。

measurements.ask: 1 kHz、50 %：示波器测 VDAC 的纹波 Vpp

measurements.explain: τ 只等于一个周期，近似公式不再适用：3.3 × tanh(T/4τ) ≈ 0.81 V，VDAC 在约 1.25 V 和 2.05 V 之间摆——已经不是直流了。
纹波 ∝ 1/f：约 8 mV，是 1 kHz 时的 1/10，平均值不变。提高 PWM 频率能减小纹波，又不会让输出变慢（τ 不变）。

hints: PWM 引脚 → 10 kΩ → VDAC；VDAC 到 GND 接 1 µF；再用跳线把 VDAC 接到一个 ADC1 引脚（GPIO32–39）。
ADC 引脚设成 ADC 模式，另一个引脚设成 PWM。
平均值 = 占空比 × 3.3 V；PWM 频率越高、RC 越大，纹波越小。
startNote: **半成品**：ESP32（GPIO27 设成 50 % PWM、GPIO34 设成 ADC）、GND 线和两个探头已经接好。**为什么**：板子是重复技能；RC 低通才是这个“DAC”。**你要做**：R1（10kΩ，GPIO27 → 第 22 列）、C1（1µF，第 22 列 → GND），再把第 22 列接到 GPIO34（j5）。
